newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN STOCKS SHOW MODERATE RISE, MORE GAINS SEEN.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN STOCKS SHOW MODERATE RISE, MORE GAINS SEEN.

text.p: Belgian shares continued higher on Tuesday after six consecutive days of gains, with good fundamentals and the prospect of dividend payouts in the weeks ahead seen keeping the market buoyant, dealers said.

"Industrials should perform well because of the low interest rates (and) I'm confident for economic recovery," one dealer said, noting the good gearing in the sector. He expected pharmaceuticals and chemicals to do well, with UCB in favour because of its positive growth forecast and Tessenderlo also liked. Retailers Colruyt and Delhaize looked expensive though, he said.
Delhaize, up 0.84 percent at 1,805 francs, suffered earlier this month after several brokers downgraded its U.S unit Food Lion amid worries about its flat sales growth.
Brokers are still waiting to see more benefits of ongoing supermarket restructuring at rival retail group GIB , up in line with the market on Monday at 1,565 francs.

By 0900 GMT the Bel-20 index of leading shares was 7.81 points or 0.36 percent higher at 2,191.01 after a mixed opening, underpinned by lower bond yields and a slight recovery in the dollar. Volume so far was a relatively low 342 million francs worth of Belgian shares.
There were already more signs of buying in baskets of Bel-20 stocks which has boosted the index and volume over the previous two sessions, dealers said.
However with the last day of the current forward market account on Wednesday, a proportion of today's activity was likely to be limited to position closing.

Several dealers said the much expected announcement late Monday that a snap election is to be held in France was having no impact on the Belgian market. "You can see how the French stock market has bounced back today," one added.
